name: Moodle LMS
summary: An open-source learning management system that institutions can self-host, obtain as a managed MoodleCloud service, or deploy through a Moodle Certified Partner. It supports course delivery, activities, assessment, communication and extensibility through plugins.

value.from: Moodle LMS software: free (self-hosted; infrastructure/support extra). MoodleCloud Starter: from $170/year for 50 users; currency/local tax should be confirmed at checkout.
value.notes: MoodleCloud plans are paid subscriptions with user/storage limits; the vendor site may localise currency by region. Hosting by certified Moodle Partners and Moodle Workplace are separately quoted.

value.freeTierNote: Yes. Moodle LMS software is open source and free to download/self-host; MoodleCloud is a paid hosted service with a free 28-day Starter trial.
value.trialNote: MoodleCloud Starter free trial for 28 days; no credit card required.

value.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA (Moodle LMS release-specific accreditation/VPAT published).
value.evidence: Moodle reports independent accessibility accreditation for specified Moodle LMS releases and publishes VPAT-based conformance information. Verify the version used by the deployment.

value.notes: AI subsystem supports configurable AI providers/plugins; model depends on administrator configuration. Provider-neutral AI subsystem: the site operator chooses and configures the AI provider, whose own data terms apply.

accessibility.finding: Accredited to WCAG 2.2 Level AA on 3 October 2025 after an external audit by GrackleDocs; a VPAT 2.5 conformance report is published. The Moodle app and Moodle Workplace are accredited separately.
accessibility.caveat: Covers the listed supported versions only. Accreditation lasts 12 months. Themes, plugins and course content are not covered.

security.finding: Moodle LMS is open-source software, so there is no product-wide SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report: security depends on who hosts it. MoodleCloud runs on AWS; AWS certifications are not Moodle's own.
security.caveat: Assess the chosen host: Moodle HQ (MoodleCloud), a Moodle Certified Partner, or the institution itself.

dataResidency.finding: Self-hosted Moodle stores data wherever the institution hosts it. MoodleCloud premium hosting can use any public AWS region, including Sydney.
dataResidency.caveat: Backups, logs, support access and third-party plugins may process data elsewhere.

ai.finding: The AI subsystem is provider-neutral: each site chooses and configures its AI provider (for example OpenAI, Azure AI or a self-hosted model), and that provider's data terms apply.
ai.caveat: There is no single Moodle-wide statement on training or retention.

procurementChecks: Hosting provider SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 certificate, DPA, subprocessor list, data centre and backup regions Site AI configuration, enabled providers, API terms, data retention and model training settings.
Current accessibility report and accreditation letter for exact version, theme and mobile app.

researchTasks: Workbook records a WCAG 2.2 AA re-accreditation on 30 Sep 2026 (versions 5.3, 5.2.3, 5.1.7, 4.5.14); on 7 Nov we could only confirm the 3 Oct 2025 accreditation. Re-open moodledev.io and update if the 2026 accreditation is listed.
Integrations need exact names: "Plugin ecosystem; LTI tools; REST/web services; SSO/SIS integrations depend on deployment and plugins.".
Commercial relationship set to none; confirm before publication (affiliate programs in docs/affiliates.md).
* security: no certification is stated, so the list is empty. Request the current security pack.
* data residency: no committed region; confirm the tenant region in the contract.
* AI models: no named model or provider, so models is empty; the description is kept as a note.

security.notes: Security posture depends on deployment and operator; Moodle HQ does not imply that every self-hosted installation is independently certified. Request hosting-provider assurance for MoodleCloud/partner hosting.

value.notes: Self-hosted: selected by customer/operator. MoodleCloud: hosted by Moodle HQ; confirm current region and plan-specific terms. For self-hosted Moodle, operator controls storage, backups and subprocessors. For MoodleCloud, review MoodleCloud terms and GDPR information.
